anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet (mcu.kicad_sch), the +12V power symbol above C1 is wired down into a junction dot that sits directly on the wire joining U6 pins 1 (DIAG_EN) and 2 (IN) to the global label HEATER. This places the raw +12V rail (and C1's top plate) on the same net as the ESP32 GPIO1 drive signal (U1 pin 13, also labeled HEATER).
anomalies.expected: The specification states that IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are driven from ESP32 GPIO1 only, and that '+12V also feeds U6 (TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) VS (pin 8) directly' — i.e. the 12 V input must not touch the control net; C1 is intended as a +12V decoupling capacitor, not a capacitor on the HEATER control net.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch (MCU sheet): '+12V' power symbol wired down to a junction dot on the wire from U6 pin 1 (DIAG_EN)/pin 2 (IN) to the global label 'HEATER'; C1 0.1uF hangs from the same node to GND

anomalies.impact: The 12 V rail is shorted to the heater control signal: U6's IN/DIAG_EN is held permanently high so the heater output is continuously energized regardless of firmware, and 12 V is back-driven into ESP32-C3 GPIO1 (a 3.3 V logic pin), which would damage the MCU and defeat the bang-bang control loop (overheating/thermal-runaway hazard).
